ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The cross-section of a fixed semicircular cylindrical glass block with radius $R$ is shown in the figure, where point $o$ is the center, and $O O^{\prime}$ is the perpendicular to the diameter MN. A sufficiently large screen $P Q$ is placed closely to the right side of the glass block and is perpendicular to MN. A beam of polychromatic light is incident along the radial direction at an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$ with respect to $O O^{\prime}$ towards point $o$. It is known that the polychromatic light contains beams with refractive indices ranging from $n_{1}=\sqrt{2}$ to $n_{2}=\sqrt{3}$, resulting in a colored band appearing on the screen.

1. What is the width of the colored light band?
2. When the angle of incidence of polychromatic light gradually increases, the colored light band on the screen will become a single light spot. What is the minimum angle $\theta$ at which this phenomenon occurs?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an upper semicircular glass cross-section, with the bottom side being the horizontal diameter MN, O on the diameter and being the center of the circle, and OO′ is a vertical dashed line through O and perpendicular to MN. The incident light is directed from the upper left along the radial direction toward O, and the angle with OO′ is marked θ; on the right side there is a vertical screen PQ, tightly against the right side of the glass block and passing through N. After the light exits from the plane MN at O, it propagates toward the lower right, and the two emergent rays in the figure respectively correspond to refraction angles β1, β2 and hit the screen on the right. Reasoning: Because the incident light enters the curved surface of the semicircle along the radial direction, at the incident point on the curved surface it is incident along the normal and no refraction occurs; dispersion only occurs on the plane MN at O. The normal direction of the plane MN is just OO′, so the angle of incidence inside the glass is θ. When θ=30°, the refraction from glass to air satisfies Snell's law: n sin θ = sin β. Calculate separately for the two ends of the refractive index range: For n1=√2, sin β1=√2·sin30°=√2/2, so β1=45°; For n2=√3, sin β2=√3·sin30°=√3/2, so β2=60°. The screen PQ is perpendicular to MN and is located at N, ON=R, so the horizontal distance from O to the screen is R. If the emergent light makes an angle β with the vertical normal, then its distance below N on the screen is R cot β. Thus the positions of the two end rays on the screen are respectively: R cot45°=R, R cot60°=R/√3. So the width of the colored light band is R-R/√3=(1-√3/3)R. When θ gradually increases, the light with the larger refractive index undergoes total internal reflection first. The minimum condition for the light band to become a single light spot is that, except for the light corresponding to the minimum refractive index n1, the rest of the light has undergone total internal reflection, while the light corresponding to n1 just reaches the critical state and grazes along the plane MN. The critical condition is n1 sin θ=1, namely √2 sin θ=1, so θ=45°.
